newsitem.title: UK: US funds turn bearish on Wall St short term - survey.
newsitem.headline: US funds turn bearish on Wall St short term - survey.

text.p: U.S. fund managers, worried about a tightening by the Federal Reserve, have turned bearish on Wall Street's short term outlook, a survey by Merrill Lynch showed.
The survey, released on Monday, said bears outnumbered bulls by 22 percent among U.S. fund managers on a three month view on U.S equities.
In last month's survey, bulls outnumbered bears by a similar number.
On a 12 month view, U.S. managers were on balance bullish, it said.

It said 61 percent of managers expect Fed Funds to rise over the coming year, up from 36 percent last month. The survey was conducted after the first part of Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's comments in the Humphrey Hawkins testimony on February 26.
U.S. managers were also no longer buyers of U.S. Treasuries, but were keen to buy Japanese equities where bulls outnumbered bears by 22 percent against four percent in the previous survey.

U.S. managers sector preferences saw sentiment for technology and energy sectors falling back, but they remained bullish on financials. The least favourite sectors were building cyclicals and ultilities.
It also said they were sellers of domestic equities, increased buyers of European equities, net sellers of UK equities, continued buyers of Pacific Basin Equities.
Latin American equities were in favour, the survey said, while they were also raising cash.
The survey was carried out by Gallup on behalf of Merrill Lynch between February 28 and March 5. It covered 41 institutions responsible for funds totalling $1,470 billion.
